sketches.title: Emotional Barometer
sketches.premise: The Host announces an ordinary weather term and a mood target. Both players write a one-line forecast that makes the mood feel inevitable without naming it. The best forecast travels farthest while remaining meteorologically possible; ceremonial thunder follows weak fronts.
sketches.criterion: The forecast must remain a plausible weather report while clearly carrying the assigned mood.
sketches.move_shape: Write one forecast sentence; example: “A warm front arrives at noon, bringing sticky hope and a ninety-percent chance of texting your ex.”
sketches.first_card: Weather term: fog; mood target: jealousy

sketches.title: Front-Page Feelings
sketches.premise: Each round gives both players the same bland headline and a hidden emotional forecast. Rewrite the headline as a tiny news alert that makes the feeling contagious without stating it. The Judge scores how dramatically the emotional weather changes while the headline still reports the same event.
sketches.criterion: The rewrite must preserve the event and headline form while making the target mood unmistakable through forecast-like detail.
sketches.move_shape: Rewrite one headline in one sentence; example: “LOCAL MAN OPENS UMBRELLA; NEIGHBORS REPORT THE SKY HAS FINALLY PICKED A SIDE.”
sketches.first_card: Headline: Dog waits outside a shop; mood: dread

sketches.title: Chance of Awkward
sketches.premise: A card gives both players an everyday situation and two harmless nouns. Turn them into a weather forecast for a mood, using both nouns exactly once. Points reward the wildest forecast that still sounds like something a weather desk could say with a straight face.
sketches.criterion: The sentence must use both nouns, forecast weather rather than narrate an event, and keep the assigned mood legible.
sketches.move_shape: Write one forecast sentence using the two nouns; example: “Scattered embarrassment will form around the sandwich, with a chance of socks by evening.”
sketches.first_card: Situation: missed bus; nouns: sandwich, socks; mood: shame

sketches.title: The Mood Map
sketches.premise: Both players receive the same place, time, and weather condition, then file a forecast that locates a mood there without naming it. The Judge rewards precise emotional geography: how much atmosphere you create before the report collapses into melodrama or nonsense.
sketches.criterion: The forecast must remain a coherent report about the given place, time, and condition while expressing the target mood indirectly.
sketches.move_shape: Write one local forecast; example: “At the school gate, clear skies will hold until the apology is expected, then visibility may drop sharply.”
sketches.first_card: Place: kitchen; time: midnight; condition: light rain; mood: loneliness

sketches.title: Pressure System
sketches.premise: The Host gives both players a plain object and a mood. Write a weather bulletin in which the object causes, predicts, or measures that mood, but never call it a symbol. The Judge applauds elegant pressure systems and clinically removes points from anyone who writes a therapy session wearing a tiny hat.
sketches.criterion: The object must function as a believable part of a weather bulletin while the bulletin makes the target mood evident without naming it.
sketches.move_shape: Write one bulletin sentence; example: “Barometric pressure is falling around the unanswered birthday card, and residents are advised not to check the mailbox.”

sketches.title: Forecast Withheld
sketches.premise: Both players get the same ordinary forecast ingredients and must write a forecast for a mood without revealing the card’s checkable truth. After both reports, each player guesses which report used the real condition most honestly. Points reward expressive misdirection: go far, but do not hand over the answer.
sketches.criterion: The forecast must preserve the given weather truth, express the assigned mood, and conceal rather than state the card’s decisive fact.
sketches.move_shape: Write one forecast sentence that uses the two nouns and avoids the forbidden fact; example: “Heavy clouds gather over the cake and doorway, with local confidence dropping by the minute.”
sketches.first_card: Weather truth: it is a birthday party; nouns: cake, doorway; mood: suspicion
